answer.evidence: The whole 16x16 cell is repeating roof tile courses. Each course runs light, mid, dark, darker (rows 1-4, 9-12), so rows 0-15 are a sloped roof plane (evidence c). The right edge (x about 11-14) is a dark strip from row 2 down. The silhouette widens 12, 13, 14, 15 over rows 0-3, which matches a diagonal hip edge, so I read it as a receding side face. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow band and no vertical south face of 3 or more rows. Rows 13-15 are just the next tile course. The cell is all roof with nothing below it, so it has no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny teal stack of horizontal slats, roughly 24x24 px at 2x. It is not a whole building: there is no roof, no walls, no door or windows, so it does not match the building kind. Measured facts show 6 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references. Near-flat coverage is 0% but only because the object is small. It has about 3 visible lightness steps on a single material, where the references have 5-6 per material with per-tile roof highlights, plaster speckle and stone shading. The outline is a tinted dark teal, not neutral black (0% near-neutral edge pixels), which is acceptable. The slat texture is a simple repeating stripe with no grain or clumping. It carries far less information than either reference and reads as a flat, sticker-like icon, not a building.

answer.evidence: The cell is a repeating roof-tile fill. Column x=4 and x=7 show courses with a light edge line at rows 1, 9 and 13, mid tones, and dark shadow rows at 4 and 12. There is no separate vertical south wall or door below the roof: rows 13-15 continue the same tile texture. So the cell shows only the sloped top surface with no front face of 3 or more rows, and it reads as a flat top-down slab.

The silhouette is 15 wide from row 3 to row 15 with no narrowing. No vertical front face (wall, door or lintel) of 3 or more rows appears below the roof planes, so the sloped roof fills the whole cell with nothing beneath it.
